scope: Read-only local implementation and retained-data investigation. Preparation only; no inference/services/imports of model libraries, package/config/source changes, downloads or staging. Iteration16 evaluated configuration is unchanged.
conclusion: The nominal 256 MiB prompt-cache byte setting is not enforced for PRISM seeded requests. The two-entry LRU count is enforced. A future one-entry arm is the smallest existing-CLI memory tradeoff experiment; it may increase prefill work and must not be treated as an adopted improvement.

confirmed_controls.claim: PRISM supplies seed=7. The server permits batching only if seed is None, so these requests use sequential _serve_single. Decode/prompt concurrency flags do not create parallel seeded inference.

run() constructs LRUPromptCache with max_size only; max_bytes defaults to 2**63. The CLI byte-budget trim is inside batched admission and is absent from _serve_single. Changing only --prompt-cache-bytes cannot bound this seeded path.

The two-entry limit is enforced at insertion. Logical retained cache reaches 0.75 decimal GB in iteration15 despite the 268435456-byte flag. Prefix lookup deep-copies cache structures; recorded logical bytes are not an independently measured allocation or total-RSS bound.

Prefill step size 256 applies to sequential generation and limits tokens in each prefill chunk, not total prompt/KV bytes. Generation clears the free allocator cache between prefill chunks. The per-request max_tokens 500 bounds generated tokens; the server CLI default is overridable by request values and is not a general memory ceiling.

Server startup and stream generation set the MLX wired limit to the device recommended working set. This is resident-memory policy, not a shared host cap. Installed MLX documentation describes the allocation memory limit as a guideline (default 1.5 times recommended working set), and the free allocator-cache limit defaults to that memory limit. Reviewed PRISM/MLX-LM paths do not explicitly lower either. Numeric live allocator limits were not queried; no MLX runtime was imported.

STT uses one shared model and one executor worker per process. Its measured queues are sub-millisecond in the three inspected suites; the slow host boundary is inside Parakeet generation. This does not exclude driver/accelerator synchronization, page movement, scheduler or thermal effects inside that boundary.

causal_limits: Iteration15 slow recognition takes 7.886798 s API-to-caller, 7.785467 s inside generation, with 0.222584 ms dispatch queue. During that call sampled available memory is about 1.407–1.713 GB; the suite minimum 0.120 GB occurs elsewhere. A suite-wide minimum is not evidence of contemporaneous exhaustion.

Iteration12 slow call is a different utterance/PCM; iteration14 and15 slow calls have different normalized PCM hashes/lengths despite both saying airport. Different raw segment bytes, background applications, warm caches and fixed run order defeat a causal historical speed comparison.
STT stages are nested host-boundary durations and may include lazy execution/synchronization. Do not sum overlapping stages or label generation time exclusive accelerator compute.

System memory/swap includes unrelated workloads and preexisting swap; half-second samples can miss peaks. Owned RSS excludes the separate recorder and is not total unified-memory allocation. Swap use levels are not measured per-process paging causation.

The earlier full-output cache comparison found a substantial one-entry prefill/latency cost. Its recorded 0.38/0.68 GB logical caches and similar sampled RSS do not establish actual memory savings or harm for this current causal RTC workload.
hypotheses_not_findings: Reducing retained KV entries may reduce pressure on the shared-memory system and recognition variability, while more prefill may instead increase compute contention/latency.
Slow generation may reflect shared accelerator/driver scheduling, page movement or background/thermal state; current artifacts do not isolate these mechanisms.

other_knobs_deferred: Do not remove seed, quantize KV, shrink/swap models, reduce max_tokens or suppress response/repair calls in this comparison.

A future explicit LRU max_bytes wrapper or MLX free-allocator-cache cap would be a separate code/runtime experiment, not evidence that today's --prompt-cache-bytes works. Lowering wired/global system limits is not proposed.

If one-entry latency regression dominates, keep two entries and separately test prefill 256→128 with otherwise identical controls; it changes temporary prefill work granularity, not retained KV budget.
